title: Principles of Data Science
author: Shaun V. Ault, et al.
description: This book bridges mathematics, programming, and business analysis, empowering you to confidently pose and address complex data questions and construct effective machine learning pipelines.

title: Machine Learning and Data Science
author: Ott Toomet
description: This book offers an accessible, hands-on introduction to the core principles of machine learning, statistical modeling, and practical data science—without overwhelming readers with complex formulas or technical jargon.

title: Mastering Data Science with C++: Performance and Innovation
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This book summarizes the essence of data science and its profound impact, while highlighting the role of the C++ language they love in supporting this field, demonstrates how C++ can be a powerful tool for data analysis and machine learning.

title: Computational and Inferential: The Foundations of Data Science
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Step by step, you'll learn how to leverage algorithmic thinking and the power of code, gain intuition about the power and limitations of current machine learning methods, and effectively apply them to real business problems.

title: Data Science: Theories, Models, Algorithms, and Analytics
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: It provides a bucket full of information regarding Data Science, covers a wide variety of sections by giving access to theories, data science algorithms, tools and analytics. You'll explore the right approach to best practices to guide you along the way.

title: The Art of Data Science
author: Roger D. Peng, et al.
description: This book describes, simply and in general terms, the process of analyzing data. This book is a distillation of authors experience in a format that is applicable to both practitioners and managers in data science.

title: Data Science and Big Data Analytics: Discovering, Analyzing, etc.
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Covers the breadth of activities, methods and tools that Data Scientists use. Focuses on concepts, principles and practical applications. The learning is supported and explained with illustrative examples using open-source software.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Machine Learning Engineers
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are deep neural networks designed for graphs with attributes attached to nodes or edges. This book introduces GNNs through the encoder-decoder framework and provides examples of decoders for a range of graph analytic tasks.

title: Mathematical Optimization for Machine Learning
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Mathematical optimization and machine learning work together because training a machine learning model relies on optimization algorithms, while optimization models can use machine learning predictions as direct inputs for decision-making.

title: Multi-Agent Technologies and Machine Learning
author: Igor Sheremet
description: This open access book discusses multi-agent technologies (MATs) and machine learning (ML). These tools can be integrated and applied in industry, commerce, energy, medicine, psychology, and other areas.

title: From Data to Intelligence: Machine Learning and AI
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This book introduces and explains essential prerequisites for understanding, applying, researching, and further developing the tools currently debated under the terms Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

title: Learning Theory from First Principles
author: Francis Bach
description: A comprehensive and cutting-edge introduction to the foundations and modern applications of learning theory. To acquire a basic mathematical understanding of the most widely used machine learning architectures.

title: Informed Machine Learning
author: Daniel Schulz, et al.
description: This open access book presents the concept of Informed Machine Learning and demonstrates its practical use with a compelling collection of applications of this paradigm in industrial and business use cases.

title: Practical Machine Learning: A Beginner's Guide with Ethical Insights
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: The book provides an accessible, comprehensive introduction for beginners to machine learning, equipping them with the fundamental skills and techniques essential for this field.

title: Algorithms For Programmers: Ideas and Source Code
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This is a book about selected algorithms. The audience in mind are programmers who are interested in the treated algorithms and actually want to create and understand working and reasonably optimized code.

title: An Open Guide to Data Structures and Algorithms
author: Paul Bible, et al
description: This textbook serves as a gentle introduction for undergraduates to theoretical concepts in data structures and algorithms in computer science while providing coverage of practical implementation (coding) issues.

title: Algorithm Design and Analysis
author: Godfrey Justo
description: This book is designed to provide you with a solid foundation in algorithmic thinking and equip you with the essential tools and techniques necessary to design and analyze efficient algorithms.

title: Algorithmic Puzzles
author: Anany Levitin, et al.
description: While many think of algorithms as specific to computer science, at its core algorithmic thinking is defined by the use of analytical logic to solve problems. This logic extends far beyond the realm of computer science and into the wide and entertaining world of puzzles.

title: Lecture Notes for the Algorithms
author: Jeff Erickson
description: This lecture notes uniquely combines rigor and comprehensiveness. It covers a broad range of algorithms in depth, yet makes their design and analysis accessible to all levels of readers. Each chapter is relatively self-contained and can be used as a unit of study.

title: The Little Book of Algorithms
author: William Lau
description: This workbook is designed to help those learning and teaching Computer Science at secondary school level. The aim of the book is to help students build fluency in their Python programming.

title: Algorithms: Fundamental Techniques
author: Macneil Shonle, et al
description: The goal of the book is to show you how you can methodically apply different techniques to your own algorithms to make them more efficient. While this book mostly highlights general techniques, some well-known algorithms are also looked at in depth.

title: Architecting a Framework for Edge Artificial Intelligence
author: Edge AI
description: This open access book presents a comprehensive exploration of the functional and non-functional requirements that define Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) systems, including technical, ethical, legal, and regulatory dimensions.

title: AiBook: A Human Survival Guide
author: Jeremy Schoemaker
description: This book is the manager's manual nobody wrote. Sixty-two short chapters, each one a pattern that keeps showing up when an agent has to do real work and not lie about it. Every chapter opens with a joke, ends with a receipt, etc.

title: Understanding Science with Large Language Models?
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: How are Large Language Models (LLMs) changing research in the history, philosophy, and sociology of science (HPSS)? Computer science develops powerful tools like LLMs, and HPSS explores the depth of their uses, limits, and broader consequences.

title: Kant and Artificial Intelligence
author: Hyeongjoo Kim, et al.
description: How are artificial intelligence (AI) and the strong claims made by their philosophical representatives to be understood and evaluated from a Kantian perspective? What can we learn from AI and its functions about Kantian philosophy’s claims to validity?

title: Open Source AI for Developers
author: Red Hat
description: This short e-book examines the compelling combination of open source and artificial intelligence (AI), showcasing the benefits of effective open source-licensed models and tools for developers.

title: Understanding Conversational AI
author: Thierry Poibeau
description: What do large language models really know-and what does it mean to live alongside them? Offer a critical and interdisciplinary exploration of large language models (LLMs), examining how they reshape our understanding of language, cognition, and society.

title: Auditing AI
author: The Marquand House Collective
description: This book explores why and how to audit artificial intelligence systems. It offers a simple roadmap for using AI audits to make product and policy changes that benefit companies and the public alike.

title: Doing Qualitative Data Analysis with NVivo
author: Dimitri Mortelmans
description: An introduction to the software program NVivo, the most widely used qualitative analysis program. It is a versatile program with an extensive range of accessible analysis tools, flexibly deployable in the diversity of qualitative analysis approaches.

title: Data Journeys in the Sciences
author: Sabina Leonelli, et al.
description: This groundbreaking, open access book analyses and compares data practices across several fields through the analysis of specific cases of data journeys. How such journeys affect the use of data as evidence and the knowledge being produced.

title: Matrix Theory and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) Apps
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is an effective method for reducing data dimensionality. Practical PCA and matrix theory translate linear algebra into workplace results. This book combines theory with real-world workplace applications across different industries.

title: Data Mining - Concepts and Applications
author: Ciza Thomas
description: The availability of big data due to computerization and automation has generated an urgent need for new techniques to analyze and convert big data into useful information and knowledge.

title: Advanced Data Analysis from an Elementary Point of View
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This is a textbook on data analysis methods, intended for advance undergraduate students who have already taken classes in probability, mathematical statistics, and linear regression. It presumes that you can read and write simple functions in R.

title: Think Stats: Exploratory Data Analysis in Python
author: Allen Downey
description: If you know how to program, you have the skills to turn data into knowledge. This thoroughly revised edition presents statistical concepts computationally, rather than mathematically, using programs written in Python

title: Data Analysis Using SQL and Excel
author: Gordon S. Linoff
description: A practical guide to data mining using SQL and Excel. Show you how to leverage the two most popular tools for data query and analysis - SQL and Excel - to perform sophisticated data analysis without the need for complex and expensive data mining tools

title: Mastering FastAPI with Python
author: Ayman Alheraki
description: This practical guide is your complete, hands-on guide to building lightning-fast, production-ready APIs using Python’s most modern web framework: FastAPI to designing, deploying, and scaling complex API architectures for real-world use.

title: Reinforcement Learning with Python
author: with Code Examples
description: Get hands-on experience in creating state-of-the-art reinforcement learning agents using TensorFlow and RLlib to solve complex real-world business and industry problems with the help of expert tips and best practices

title: Beej's Guide to Python Programming
author: Brian Hall
description: This book is designed with you in mind. It understands that you might be coming from a completely different background, maybe feeling a little intimidated by all the tech jargon out there.

title: Introduction to Programming and Computer Science with Python
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This book is for everyone who is interested in deepening their understanding, not only of the Python language, but also of practical computer science. Best Python book for intermediate level users.

title: Learn Python with Jupyter
author: Serena Bonaretti
description: In this open access book, you will learn to code in Python using Jupyter Notebook. Even more importantly, you will develop computational thinking, which is the way we think when coding.

title: Object-Oriented Programming in Python
author: M. H. Goldwasser
description: An intuitive and thorough guide to mastering object-oriented programming from the ground up. Cover the basics of building classes and creating objects, and put theory into practice with clear examples that help visualize the object-oriented style.

title: Microcontroller Programming with Arduino and Python
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This book provides the solid foundation to start your journey of embedded systems development and microcontroller programming with Arduino and Python, explains how to conduct Arduino experiments using Arduino IDE and Python

title: Modern C++ From Zero to Professional
author: Ayman Alheraki
description: The book is designed specifically to focus on the fundamentals of C++ in a detailed, structured, and comprehensive way, while still maintaining a clear path toward professional-level expertise.

title: From C to Modern C++
author: Ayman Alheraki
description: The book shows that Modern C++ is best learned not by forgetting C, but by building on its strengths and correcting its pain points, therefore avoids repeating basic programming concepts and concentrates on the conceptual and engineering transition to C++.

title: Modern C++ Debugging: Principles to Advanced Diagnostics
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This book is a practical guide with examples, provides a comprehensive introduction to identifying, understanding, and resolving the multitude of errors and issues that can arise in C++ programming, not merely to list tools and commands.

title: Mastering Regular Expressions in Modern C++
author: Ayman Alheraki
description: The objective of this booklet is to present regular expressions as a precise engineering tool within Modern C++. The focus on correct usage, clarity of implementation, and real-world applicability.

title: Network Programming in C++
author: Ayman Alheraki
description: This book is written for C++ developers who seek a deep and accurate understanding of network programming from a systems-oriented perspective, rather than through highlevel frameworks, convenience libraries.

title: Mastering Object-Oriented Programming in Modern C++
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This book was written with a single goal in mind: to help developers, both novice and experienced, understand the principles of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) and Modern C++ in a structured, practical, and accessible manner.

title: C++ Mastery: From Fundamentals to Embedded Systems
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Designed for seasoned C++ programmers, this book delves beyond foundational concepts, empowering you to unleash the full potential of this versatile language. Professional C++ Learning Curriculum - From Fundamentals to Embedded Systems.

title: JavaScript Frameworks/Libraries
author: React.js, Angular, Node.js, etc.
description: A collection of JavaScript Frameworks/Libraries related books, including (but not limited to): React.js, Angular/AngularJS, Node.js, Vue.js, Backbone.js, Ember.js, Knockout.js, Dojo.js, D3.js, Three.js, Leaflet.js, Google Maps API, Bing Maps API, etc.

title: Learning Patterns: Web Apps with vanilla JavaScript and React
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Patterns are time-tested templates for writing code. In this book, you will learn design patterns, performance and rendering patterns for building high-quality web applications using modern JavaScript and React.

title: JavaScript Simplified
author: Taye Abidakun
description: This book begins by teaching you the JavaScript language from the ground up. Then it takes you beyond the fundamentals, so you understand and learn to use advanced programming features.

title: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition: A Modern Introduction
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Eloquent JavaScript dives deep into the JavaScript language to show you how to write beautiful, effective code. It immerses you in example code from the start, while exercises and full-chapter projects give you hands-on experience.

title: JavaScript for Impatient Programmers
author: Axel Rauschmayer
description: This book makes JavaScript less challenging to learn for newcomers, by offering a modern view that is as consistent as possible. No prior knowledge of JavaScript is required, but you should know how to program.

title: JavaScript from Zero to Hero
author: Rick Sekuloski
description: Whether you're a complete beginner or a coder looking to deepen your knowledge, this book is your gateway to mastering JavaScript, the most essential language of the web. Unlock your web development superpowers!

title: Deep JavaScript: Theory and Techniques
author: Axel Rauschmayer
description: In depth knowledge of JavaScript makes it easier to learn a variety of other frameworks, including Node.js, React, Angular, and related tools and libraries. This book is designed to help you cover the core JavaScript concepts you need to build modern applications.

title: How to Lie with Statistics
author: Darrell Huff
description: This book is a brief, breezy illustrated volume outlining the misuse of statistics and errors in the interpretation of statistics, and how errors create incorrect conclusions. It also shows how statistical graphs can be used to distort reality.

title: Understanding Statistics and Experimental Design
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Provide the background needed to correctly use, interpret and understand statistics and statistical data in diverse settings. Readers with little or no background in statistics will appreciate how these fundamental concepts are so well illustrated.

title: Basic Statistics Using R for Crime Analysis
author: Jaeyong Choi
description: This book is for those interested in becoming crime analysts, focusing on learning statistics without delving too deeply into mathematics. Emphasizes practical applications by utilizing R for data analysis, etc..

title: Statistics Minus The Math: An Introduction for the Social Sciences
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: This book is a true introduction, not assuming any prior training in statistics. It minimizes use of math (beyond the very elementary) in initial explanations, instead focusing on conceptual description and interpretation.

title: Learning Statistics with Jamovi: A Tutorial for Statistical Analysis
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Covers the analysis of contingency tables, t-tests, correlation, regression, ANOVA and factor analysis, giving a firm grounding in descriptive statistics and graphing. It includes learning aids for applying statistical principles using the Jamovi interface, etc.

title: Understanding Statistics: An Introduction
author: Antony Davies
description: This book gives you the tools to understand statistical claims and avoid common pitfalls associated with translating statistical information from the language of mathematics to plain English.

title: Elementary Statistics: A Step By Step Approach
author: Allan Bluman
description: A beginning statistics course for students whose mathematical background is limited to basic algebra. Follows a non-theoretical approach without formal proofs, explaining concepts intuitively and supporting them with abundant examples.

title: Introduction to Calculus
author: J. H. Heinbockel
description: This textbook is an introductory calculus presentation intended for future scientists and engineers. Be sure that you have had the appropriate background material of algebra and trigonometry.

title: Understanding Basic Calculus
author: S. K. Chung
description: This textbook is an introductory calculus presentation intended for future scientists and engineers. Be sure that you have had the appropriate background material of algebra and trigonometry.

title: Fractional Calculus: Theory and Applications
author: Jorge E Macías Díaz
description: Fractional Calculus has led to tremendous progress in various areas of science and mathematics. New definitions of fractional derivatives and integrals have been uncovered, extending their classical definitions in various ways.

title: The Fractional Calculus: Theory and Applications
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Not only does it explain the theory (Fractional Calculus) underlying the properties of the generalized operator, but it also illustrates the wide variety of fields to which these ideas may be applied.

title: Calculus Made Easy
author: Silvanus P. Thompson
description: This book is a popular math book to help modern readers of all levels understand the subject on calculus through simple way and explanation. It's not just theory-based but contains exercises and answers so you can practice the understanding for each chapter.

title: Exercises and Problems in Calculus
author: John M. Erdman
description: Ideal for self-instruction as well as for classroom use, this text helps students improve their understanding and problem-solving skills in analysis, analytic geometry, and higher algebra.

title: Teaching and Learning of Calculus
author: David Bressoud, et al.
description: Focuses on the main trends in the field of calculus education. Despite their variety, the findings reveal a cornerstone issue that is strongly linked to the formalism of calculus concepts and to the difficulties it generates in the learning and teaching process.

title: Mastering Linux: From Zero to Advanced Expertise
author: Ayman Alheraki
description: A single unifying goal: to transform the reader from a casual user into a fully competent expert capable of understanding, configuring, administering, programming, and extending modern Linux systems—with precision and confidence.

title: Linux Fundamentals
author: Paul Cobbaut
description: This book provides a soft, accessible, and practical introduction to Linux environments and command line basics, from a basic approach to Linux to a more advanced server-oriented look at using Linux.

title: Linux for Beginners
author: Jason Cannon
description: This book discusses the ins and outs of Linux in a beginner friendly style to make your learning process frustration free, includes Command Line, Programming and Operating System, as the book does not assume you know anything about Linux.

title: Just Enough Linux
author: Malcolm Maclean
description: This book aims at getting you comfortable with some of the commands used in Linux. If you've toyed with Linux and never really caught on to what's happening or have used a graphical interface without really touching the command line this book is for you.

title: Linux with Operating System Concepts
author: Richard Fox
description: This book merges conceptual operating system (OS) and Unix/Linux topics into one cohesive textbook for undergraduate students, covers Linux from both the user and system administrator positions.

title: Linux Basics for Hackers: Networking, Scripting, and Security in Kali
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Uses the Kali Linux distribution to teach Linux basics with a focus on how hackers would use them. Topics include Linux command line basics, filesystems, networking, BASH basics, package management, logging, and the Linux kernel and drivers.

title: Kali Linux Revealed: Mastering the Penetration Testing Distribution
author: Multiple Contributors / Open Curriculum
description: Kali Linux has not only become the information security professional's platform of choice, but evolved into an industrial-grade, and world-class operating system distribution--mature, secure, and enterprise-ready.
